opening_message:
Ticket 1: Douglas Salinas (employee ID E045) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E045.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Douglas Salinas (E045) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Payroll; full-time employees may have up to write, and admin is not permitted since Engineer does not own Payroll. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for E045 shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. With basic training, maximum access is read. Requested write, so grant read.
reason: The Security record for E045 shows Douglas Salinas is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training, and never admin. With basic training, the maximum allowed level is read. Although the HR note lists him as full-time, the contractor status from the security record restricts access, and read is the level that does not exceed the maximum under either interpretation. The requested write exceeds the maximum, so I grant the maximum: read.
